to-the-grave.about: The album opener: mournful, accusatory and affectionate at once. Roads, departure and mortality establish Hovercraft’s recurring escape vocabulary immediately.
to-the-grave.archive: The surviving 1996 original is an extended form of the song, with two additional verses and a final chorus. The 2026 reconstruction condenses that longer structure; some musical DNA can also be traced to a pre-Hovercraft retro-space pop band jam.

evidence.label: Master-tape note
evidence.caption: Handwritten tape details dated 29 May 1996: part of the surviving source-recording trail.

to-the-grave.lyrics_artwork_alt: A collage of handwritten song lyrics titled Hovercraft To The Grave, vintage photos, clocks, and various old paper scraps creating a nostalgic and melancholic atmosphere.

mr-tooting-brown.about: An affectionate and grotesque portrait of a faded rock ’n’ roll fantasist: absurd, self-mythologising and still somehow loved.
mr-tooting-brown.archive: The 2026 recording was reconstructed from the original 1995 studio demo. A later solo acoustic performance by Gol led to a separate 2025 reconstruction.

evidence.label: Handwritten song sheet
evidence.caption: Original chord and structure sheet for Mr Tooting Brown.

versions.label: Early pre-drummer version
versions.title: Mr Tooting Brown ft. Dr. Rhythm
versions.source: Boss DR-550 Dr. Rhythm · early October 1995

versions.label: Acoustic reconstruction source
versions.title: Mr Tooting Brown — Gol acoustic rendition
versions.note: Used as the source for the 2025 Shaken Not Stirred reconstruction after direct attempts from the original Hovercraft demos and 4-tracks failed to produce a recognisable recreation.

mr-tooting-brown.lyrics_artwork_alt: A vintage rock 'n' roll-themed setup features a poster of Mr. Tooting Brown, a man in sunglasses and a leather jacket, alongside a crown, a vinyl record, handwritten lyrics, a bottle labeled Rock 'N' Roll, and a syringe on a rustic wooden table.

white-limousine.about: A compact cinematic escape fantasy, moving from bruised morning-after imagery towards an extravagant promise of departure. The limousine can suggest rescue, luxury, wedding, funeral or simple excess.

evidence.label: Original set list
evidence.caption: Period set list naming White Limousine alongside Cool Jerk, Oh Yeah, New Pine Overcoat, Crazy and others.

versions.label: Later Piers version
versions.title: White Limousine
versions.note: A later Piers version of the Hovercraft composition, preserved in the Boscombe Philosophical Orchestra catalogue.

white-limousine.lyrics_artwork_alt: A vintage white limousine is parked on a dimly lit street with retro neon signs and a collage of handwritten song lyrics, photographs, and a glass of whiskey in the foreground.

crazy.about: An accusation that keeps collapsing into obsession. The song tries to turn desire into conquest and possession, only to discover that contempt is no cure for attraction.

evidence.label: Handwritten lyric draft
evidence.caption: Early lyric draft showing Crazy taking shape, including revisions and discarded material.

crazy.lyrics_artwork_alt: The image features a grungy, vintage-looking collage with song lyrics titled CRAZY, a black-and-white photo of a woman with tears, an ashtray with cigarette butts, pills labeled CRAZY PILLS, a lipstick, and various labeled items including a ticket and a badge with phrases like ROCK 'N' ROLL IS REAL BIZARRE and ATMOSPHERE IS EVERYTHING.

concrete-hill.about: One of Hovercraft’s clearest social landscapes: estate life, buses, fighting, weekends, bodily comedy and aspiration collide with the desire to escape place, class and self.
concrete-hill.archive: The surviving 1996 demo is longer, darker and more exploratory.

versions.label: Later Piers version
versions.title: Concrete Hill
versions.note: A later Piers version of the Hovercraft composition, preserved in the Boscombe Philosophical Orchestra catalogue.

evidence.label: Archive track list
evidence.caption: Handwritten archive list naming Concrete Hill among the original repertoire.

concrete-hill.lyrics_artwork_alt: A weathered, nostalgic collage features handwritten lyrics titled Concrete Hill, a vintage bus ticket, an old photo, a can of Tennent's lager, sunglasses, and an urban outdoor scene with people in the background.

superman.about: A tiny rush of work, intoxication and comic-book escape. The narrator rejects the burden of being a hero while keeping the fantasy of power and flight.

evidence.label: Handwritten song sheet
evidence.caption: Original Superman music and chord sheet.

versions.label: 1996 live segue · 4-track
versions.title: Superman → These Days
versions.note: The songs were often segued together live.

superman.lyrics_artwork_alt: A vintage, gritty collage features the word SUPERMAN, handwritten poetic lyrics about wanting to be a hero and fly, an old telephone booth, urban city scenes, and a glass of whiskey on the rocks.

these-days.about: A satire of revolutionary certainty ageing into cars, holidays, domestic comfort and postponed revolution. Its saving move is self-implication: the singer has changed too.
these-days.archive: The surviving source material came from different versions at different speeds, including an 8-track master-tape source that was backwards. That the song survives in recoverable form at all is remarkable.

versions.label: 1996 live segue · 4-track
versions.title: Superman → These Days
versions.note: The songs were often segued together live.

versions.label: Archival reconstruction source
versions.title: These Days — rehearsal source
versions.note: Two versions out of sync; one source was backwards at half speed. This composite was used for the later reconstruction.

these-days.lyrics_artwork_alt: A vintage-style collage features lyrics from the song These Days by Madness, a cityscape with a man relaxing, a classic car with keys, and various handwritten notes and quotes.

killer-blues.about: Short, nasty and funny garage/pub blues. Riff and attitude do as much work as conventional structure.

evidence.label: Handwritten structure sheet
evidence.caption: Original Killer Blues chord and arrangement sheet.

evidence.label: Handwritten lyric draft
evidence.caption: Original lyric draft with corrections and crossed-out material.

killer-blues.lyrics_artwork_alt: The image is a gritty collage featuring the title Killer Blues with handwritten lyrics or poetry, sepia-toned photos of urban scenes and a toilet, and elements like whiskey bottles, pills, and notes conveying themes of despair, addiction, and loss.

pass-the-night-nurse.about: A chemical comedown that opens outward into an anti-authoritarian rant. Its strangest imagery imagines humanity as a single damaged organism.

versions.label: Early pre-drummer version
versions.title: Pass The Night Nurse ft. Dr. Rhythm
versions.source: Boss DR-550 Dr. Rhythm · early October 1995

pass-the-night-nurse.lyrics_artwork_alt: A vintage-style collage featuring a bottle of Night Nurse cough medicine, handwritten notes and lyrics about coping with trauma, a prescription label, and various messages related to drug use, mental health, and social issues.

new-pine-overcoat.about: A hopeful road song with a black-joke reveal: the title points towards a coffin, retrospectively poisoning much of the optimism that precedes it.
new-pine-overcoat.archive: The 1996 demo is slower, barer and more psychologically exposed. The song was also reworked in 2025 as The Promised Land.

versions.label: Later Piers version
versions.title: New Pine Overcoat
versions.note: A later Piers version of the Hovercraft composition, preserved in the Boscombe Philosophical Orchestra catalogue.

new-pine-overcoat.lyrics_artwork_alt: A group of four people are gathered in a dimly lit room, playing guitars and surrounded by various music-related memorabilia and handwritten lyrics.

cool-jerk.about: Hovercraft’s route into the song runs from The Capitols through The Creation. The band leans into The Creation’s British freakbeat and mod aggression and turns it into damaged pub-band electricity.
cool-jerk.archive: Lineage: The Capitols → The Creation → Hovercraft.

evidence.label: Original set list
evidence.caption: Period set list with Cool Jerk crossed out — a small surviving trace of the live repertoire changing in real time.

sweet-thing.about: Gentle reassurance with unease underneath it. Patience, time and distance make it a quiet reset after the covers, while its road imagery echoes New Pine Overcoat.
sweet-thing.lyrics_artwork_alt: A vintage-style collage features a sepia-toned photo of a contemplative woman sitting by a window, surrounded by handwritten lyrics titled Sweet Thing, a pocket watch, a dried rose, and motivational phrases about time and patience.

keep-it-together.about: An exposed apology that refuses to become a model apology. Remorse, self-pity, evasion and damage remain tangled together, and the song denies itself a neat resolution.
keep-it-together.lyrics_artwork_alt: A distressed person sits alone on a bench in a dimly lit area at night, surrounded by handwritten notes expressing feelings of pain, loneliness, and self-doubt with phrases like KEEP IT TOGETHER, I'M IN PIECES, and I JUST CAN'T SEEM TO LOOK THEM IN THE EYE.

i-love-you-and-i.about: A blunt plea built from love, dependence and fear. By the end, presence matters more than rescue.
i-love-you-and-i.archive: The final performance makes a small but emotionally significant conjunction change in its closing refrain.

versions.label: 2025 recording
versions.title: I Love You (And I Don't Want You To Die)

versions.label: 33 Weelsby Road · live 4-track
versions.title: I Love You (And I Don't Want You To Die)

i-love-you-and-i.lyrics_artwork_alt: A vintage scrapbook page features heartfelt lyrics titled I LOVE YOU AND I DON'T WANT YOU TO DIE, alongside sepia-toned photos of a couple, a glass of whiskey, a pocket watch, and scattered notes with emotional phrases.

indie-kid.about: It starts as scene satire — clothes, magazines, parties and poses — then curdles into something closer to elegy, pulling the caricature back into English weather, place and loss.

evidence.label: Original set list
evidence.caption: Period set list grouping Indie Kid with Killer Blues and Superman.

indie-kid.lyrics_artwork_alt: A grungy collage features lyrics from the song Indie Kid, vintage black-and-white photos, a cigarette-filled ashtray, and references to punk culture such as Teen Beat magazine and Teenage Wasteland.

now-youre-god-dying-comes.about: The album’s largest set-piece: public worship, stardom and unstable godhood collapse into private mortality.
now-youre-god-dying-comes.archive: The 2026 recording is a stitched construction assembled from three reconstructed parts.

versions.label: 2025 recording
versions.title: Now You're God / Dying Comes So Easy

versions.label: 33 Weelsby Road · live 4-track
versions.title: Now You're God / Dying Comes So Easy

now-youre-god-dying-comes.lyrics_artwork_alt: A dark-themed collage features handwritten song lyrics titled Now You're God and Dying Comes So Easy, with photos, a crown, backstage passes, a cassette tape, a dried rose, a razor blade, and a headline about a rock star's death.

take-it-or-leave-it.about: Hovercraft’s nearest thing to a manifesto: anti-violence, anti-persecution, suspicious of grand ideology and reaching towards solidarity. Its awkward slogans remain part of the historical song.

evidence.label: Handwritten song sheet
evidence.caption: Original music and structure sheet for Take It Or Leave It.

versions.label: Later Piers version
versions.title: Take It Or Leave It
versions.note: A later Piers version of the Hovercraft composition, preserved in the Boscombe Philosophical Orchestra catalogue.

take-it-or-leave-it.lyrics_artwork_alt: A vintage-style collage features handwritten lyrics titled Take It or Leave It, a photograph of a road with a Follow the Sun sign, peace symbols, and messages promoting love, unity, and non-violence.

here-now.about: The emotional ending of Doomed To Live. After an album full of roads and escape, it turns towards presence and repair instead.
here-now.archive: Piers wrote the song in 2009 and sent Gol the original recording on CD. Gol's 2014 rendition was based on that recording and later became the source for both the 2025 Shaken Not Stirred reconstruction and Gol's 2026 Suno rendition. Piers later published his version through the Boscombe Philosophical Orchestra in 2015; that recording became the source for the Oh Yeah reconstruction.

versions.label: Source rendition
versions.title: Here Now — Gol
versions.note: Based on Piers' 2009 recording. This 2014 rendition became the source for both the 2025 Shaken Not Stirred reconstruction and Gol's 2026 Suno rendition.

versions.label: Source recording
versions.title: Here Now — Piers / Boscombe Philosophical Orchestra
versions.source: Boscombe Philosophical Orchestra · Bandcamp publication of Piers' earlier version
versions.note: Used as the source for the later Oh Yeah album reconstruction.

versions.label: 2026 Gol version
versions.title: Here Now — Gol
versions.note: Suno-generated from Gol's 2014 rendition; a second descendant of that source alongside the 2025 Shaken Not Stirred reconstruction.

video.label: The Magpies · Here Now · 2012
video.note: Piers performing Here Now with The Magpies in 2012. The only surviving video currently known of any of the musicians playing one of these songs.

here-now.lyrics_artwork_alt: A vintage-style collage features the handwritten lyrics to the song Here Now surrounded by notes, a coffee cup, a pen, a guitar pick, and sepia-toned photographs of a rainy window and a messy bed.

oh-yeah.type: Original song incorporating a borrowed refrain
oh-yeah.about: It enters through a familiar blues and R&B doorway and then becomes another song: borrowed bravado gives way to failed potency and increasingly manic self-exposure.
oh-yeah.archive: The borrowed refrain is omitted from the published song text.

evidence.label: Original set list
evidence.caption: Period set list documenting Oh Yeah in the original Hovercraft repertoire.

oh-yeah.lyrics_artwork_alt: A vintage-style scene featuring a voodoo doll, a record player with a spinning vinyl, a seductive black-and-white pin-up photo marked with lipstick kisses, and various weathered objects, all set against a graffiti-covered wall with handwritten notes.

bring-my-baby-back.about: A rockabilly/pub-rock sprint with a sideways gait. Comic romantic panic, speed and factory-life texture give it a distinctly Hovercraft form of vulnerability.
bring-my-baby-back.archive: The band’s 1995–96 listening world included The Clash’s Jimmy Jazz — useful context for the feel, without making the song an imitation.

versions.label: 2025 recording
versions.title: Bring My Baby Back To Me

versions.label: 33 Weelsby Road · live 4-track
versions.title: Bring My Baby Back — alternative version

bring-my-baby-back.lyrics_artwork_alt: A vintage-style collage features a distressed man walking by a No Vacancy hotel sign, a torn missing person poster asking for help to find my baby, handwritten lyrics titled BRING MY BABY BACK, a vinyl record, and a shot glass, all conveying a theme of loss and longing.

low.about: Exile, failed stardom, gear, disappointment and the need for guidance gather around the image of a bottle and a suitcase — the phrase that supplied the companion album’s former working title.
low.archive: A known older web transcription contains one corrected word.

evidence.label: Handwritten structure sheet
evidence.caption: Original structure/chord chart, identified with high confidence as Low.

low.lyrics_artwork_alt: A notebook page with handwritten lyrics titled LOW, accompanied by photographs, guitar picks, and torn notes expressing themes of loneliness and heartbreak.

my-own-little-world.about: Gentle folk-rock with a cyclical feel and a faint Bo Diddley undertow. Warmth and mutual shelter coexist with a slight possessive anxiety.
my-own-little-world.lyrics_artwork_alt: A collage of handwritten lyrics, drawings, photographs, and mementos revolves around the theme My Own Little World by Hovercraft.

bob-bob-bob.about: An elegy whose force comes from tiny human detail rather than grand tragedy. Grief eventually narrows to an absurdly small unpaid debt, funny and brutal at the same time.
bob-bob-bob.archive: A genuine 1995–96 Hovercraft song for which no complete original band performance has yet surfaced. Piers' 2015 Boscombe Philosophical Orchestra recording survives and became the source for the Oh Yeah album reconstruction.

evidence.label: Original Bob Bob Bob working page
evidence.caption: The title is written across the top above the chord and arrangement notes; the lower half is filled with repeated HOVERCRAFT logo sketches.

versions.label: Source recording
versions.title: Bob Bob Bob — Piers / Boscombe Philosophical Orchestra
versions.note: Used as the source for the Oh Yeah album reconstruction.

versions.label: Additional Piers version
versions.title: Bob Bob Bob
versions.note: A further later version preserved in Piers' Boscombe Philosophical Orchestra catalogue.

bob-bob-bob.lyrics_artwork_alt: A handwritten note featuring lyrics or a poem titled Bob Bob Bob, surrounded by nostalgic items including a worn photo, a David Bowie LP cover, a bottle of Old Crow whiskey, and a sketched portrait.

season-of-the-witch.about: Hovercraft approaches Donovan’s composition through the Julie Driscoll, Brian Auger & The Trinity interpretation, roughening its jazz-psych tension into something heavier and warier.
season-of-the-witch.archive: The retained studio comment at the end returns the listener to musicians in a room rather than polishing away the evidence.

evidence.label: Original set list
evidence.caption: Period set list documenting Season Of The Witch in Hovercraft’s live repertoire.

angel.about: One of the companion album’s emotional peaks: grief, defiance, attempted rebirth and petty revenge are allowed to remain messy rather than resolving cleanly.
angel.archive: The finished recording joins two different reconstructed versions. The audible seam and room remarks remain deliberately as part of its material history.

evidence.label: Handwritten song sheet
evidence.caption: Original Angel chord and structure sheet.

angel.lyrics_artwork_alt: A vintage-style collage features handwritten lyrics titled ANGEL, a teddy bear with a tag, a black-and-white photograph of a person in a rainy street, an electric guitar, matches, a lighter, a dried flower, an access pass, and a journal labeled Kurt Cobain Journals.

the-promised-land.credit: Lyrics by Piers "Charlie Pepper" Wildman & David Marsden
the-promised-land.about: A 2025 reworking of New Pine Overcoat: the same underlying song viewed through a different recording and arrangement. It keeps the road-song momentum but inverts the original song’s dark destination.
the-promised-land.archive: Related composition: New Pine Overcoat. Kept as a distinct published song page because the 2025 reworking has its own recording history.

in-the-midnight-hour.about: Hovercraft's version of the soul standard survives as part of the original rehearsal-room archive. Unlike the other recovered repertoire, it was not recreated in the later Suno sessions because the service's copyright filter prevented the attempt.
in-the-midnight-hour.archive: Recorded live at the 33 Weelsby Road Hovercraft rehearsal room on 4-track in 1996. The surviving original is therefore the central recording evidence for this song.

ill-make-love-to-you.about: Hovercraft takes J.J. Cale’s laconic composition and pushes it towards something more urgent and garage-like. The interest here is arrangement and performance.

versions.label: 33 Weelsby Road · live 4-track
versions.title: I'll Make Love To You Anytime
